rows.speaker: سعدى
rows.claim: Saʿdī’s Persian poem presents death as a summons to leave and urges friends to say farewell, while the speaker regrets his own unpreparedness.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدى) : كوس رحلت بكوفت دست أجل

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yaḥyā b. Muʿādh reports that four angels address the dead at the grave: lifespans and hopes are gone, wealth leaves deeds behind, worldly concerns leave consequences, and lawful earning and service to God bring felicity.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ رحمه الله إذا دخل الميت القبر قام على شفير قبره أربعة أملاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death’s distress, the person’s leg turns around or joins the other; ساق here first denotes the bodily limb.
rows.anchor: أي والتفت ساقه بساقه والتوت عليها عند قلق الموت فالساق العضو المخصوص

rows.speaker: سعيد بن امسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib takes the two ساقs to be the dead person’s legs when they are wrapped in the shroud.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن امسيب هما سقاه حين تلفان في أكفائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase figures the hardship of leaving this world meeting the hardship of entering the next; ساق became a metaphor for crisis because a person bares his legs to face a severe task.
rows.anchor: أو التفت شدة فراق الدنيا بشدة إقبال الآخرة على أن الساق مثل في الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person is driven to God and His judgment, where no one else has authority to rule.
rows.anchor: أي إلى الله وإلى حكمه يساق الإنسان لا إلى غيره أي يساق إلى حيث لا حكم هناك إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المساق is a verbal noun of driving, expressed in Persian as being driven.
rows.anchor: فالمساق مصدر ميمي بمعنى السوق بالفارسية راندن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in المساق substitutes for a genitive complement, meaning the driving of the human being.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام عوض عن المضاف إليه أي سوق الإنسان

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī glosses the destination as the return of everyone to the recompense of their Lord.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) : بسوى جزاى رورد كارتو آروز باز كشت باشد همه كس را

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person did not affirm what must be believed about the Messenger and the Qurʾān revealed to him.
rows.anchor: الإنسان ما يجب تصديقه من الرسول والقرآن الذي نزل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here لا has the force of لم with a past verb; Arabic commonly repeats لا in paired negation, while using it alone is rare.
rows.anchor: فلا ههنا بمعنى لم وإنما دخلت على الماضي لقوة التكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading is that he did not give the alms due on his wealth, with فلا صدق ماله understood as withholding zakāt.
rows.anchor: أو فلا صدق ماله بمعنى لا زكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If صدق means zakāt, its mention before prayer suits Meccans’ withholding from the needy and failure to urge feeding during acute need; prayer comes later to preserve the verse endings.
rows.anchor: ولعل وجهه ما كان كفار مكة عليه من منع المساكين وعدم الحض على طعامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He did not perform the prayer made obligatory for him.
rows.anchor: ما فرض عليه وفيه دلالة على أن الكفار مخاطبون بالفروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that unbelievers are accountable for subsidiary religious duties in punishment: a disbeliever merits blame and punishment for abandoning prayer as for abandoning faith, though worldly performance is not required of him.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن الكفار مخاطبون بالفروع في حق المؤاخذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejected what had been conveyed about the Messenger and the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: ما ذكر من الرسول والقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولكن prevents an inference that failure to affirm necessarily means outright denial: doubt lies between belief and denial, so this clause adds a distinct fact rather than repeating the previous one.
rows.anchor: والاستدراك لدفع احتمال الشك فإن نفي التصديق لا يستلزم إثبات التكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned away from obedience and from the Messenger.
rows.anchor: {وتولى} واعرض عن الطاعةولرسوله {ثم ذهب إلى أهله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أهله may mean his household or his companions.
rows.anchor: أهل بيته أو إلى أصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He walked swaggering and strutting proudly, boasting of his denial and turning away.
rows.anchor: يتبختر ويختال في مشيه افتخارا بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation is from المط, stretching: the swaggerer lengthens his stride, so the word is a metaphor for strutting; its expected form يتمطط changes the last ط to ي to avoid identical adjacent consonants.
rows.anchor: من المط وهو المد فإن المتبختر يمد خطاه يعني أن التمدد في المشي من لوازم التبختر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second derivation takes it from المطا, the back: the strutter twists and moves his back, with the alif substituted for wāw.
rows.anchor: أو من المطا مقصورا وهو الظهر فإنه يلويه ويحركه في تبختره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يتمطى is a circumstantial clause describing the subject of ذهب.
rows.anchor: ويتمطى جمة حالية من فاعل ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited hadith uses المطيطاء for swaggering with an extended gait and arms; البأس means the severity of battle.
rows.anchor: التبختر ومد اليدين في المشي والبأص شدة الحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أولى لك is a threat wishing that what he dislikes draw near; it is used in the sense of ويل لك, “woe to you.”
rows.anchor: فهو مستعمل في موضع ويل لك مشتق من الولي وهو القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated formula intensifies the threat.
rows.anchor: تكرير للتأكيد فهو مستعمل في موضع ويل لك مشتق من الولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat may derive from “May God bring near to you what you hate,” with an added lām and a triliteral form shifted to ifʿāl to take two objects.
rows.anchor: وأصله أولاك الله ما تكرهه واللام مزيدة كما في ردف لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs gives two explanations: a warning that destruction approaches, or a noun meaning destruction is more fitting and preferable for you.
rows.anchor: أولى لك تهديد ووعيد أي قاربه ما يهلكه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī assigns the repetitions escalating fates: a hard death, painful grave punishment, the horrors of resurrection, then eternal residence in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) : أولى لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forty days the semen becomes, by God’s power, a thick, dark-red clinging clot, having been white fluid; the commentary links this sequence to 23:14.
rows.anchor: أي ثم كان لمني بعد أربعين يوما قطعة دم جامد غليظ أحمر بقدرة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After another forty days it becomes flesh capable of differentiation into organs; God makes bones, covers them with flesh to perfect form and prepare it for powers and the spirit, then proportionately fashions it.
rows.anchor: جعلها مضغة مخلقة بعد أربعين أخرى أي قطعة لحم قابل لتفريق الأعضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فسوى means that God proportioned and perfected the creature’s formation.
rows.anchor: فكسا العظام لحما يحسن به خلقه وتصويره

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī glosses the phrase as forming the person’s shape and limbs and breathing the spirit into him.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي) : س رلست كردصورت واندام اورا وووح دردميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mufradāt explains perfecting as making the creature’s formation conform to divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: وفي المفرات جعل خلقه على ما اقتضته الحكمة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes proportioning to mean matching each paired bodily organ with its counterpart.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : معنى التسوية والتعديل جعل كل عضو من أعضائه الزوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منه may mean from humanity as a class or from semen; جعل means “created” and therefore takes one object, الزوجين.
rows.anchor: أي من الإنسان باعتبار الجنس أو من المني وجعل بمعنى خلق ولذا اكتفى بمفعول واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذكر والأنثى can stand in apposition to الزوجين or be accusatives under an implied أعني, “I mean.”
rows.anchor: بدل من الزوجين ويجوز أن يكونا منصوبين بإضمار أعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ف marks sequence, the clauses must differ in stage: the first may describe a formative period enabling sex differentiation, and the second the actual distinction into male and female.
rows.anchor: فلعل قوله فخلق فسوى محمول على مقدار مقدر من الخلق يصلح به للتفرقة بين الزوجين

words: أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who made this remarkable creation can raise the dead; rationally, resurrection is easier than origination because primordial matter and the original elements remain.
rows.anchor: وهو أهون من البدء في قياس العقل لوجود المادة وهو عجب الذنب والعناصر الأصلية

words: أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى
rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet would answer the verse when reciting it, “Glory be to You, O God—indeed”; another version has him repeat “Indeed, by God” twice, affirming resurrection and God’s power.
rows.anchor: أن النبي عليه السلام كان إذا قرأها قال سبحانك اللهم بلى

words: أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a reciter of al-Aʿlā should say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High,” and at the end of al-Qiyāmah should say “Glory be to You, O God—indeed,” whether leading prayer or not.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما من قرأ سبح اسم ربك الأعلى إما ما كان أو غيره

words: أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith instructs reciters of al-Tīn, al-Qiyāmah, and al-Mursalāt to answer their closing questions with affirmation and witness, “Glory be to You—indeed,” and “We believe in God,” respectively.
rows.anchor: من قرأ منكم والتين والزيتون فانتهى إلى آخرها أليس بالله بأحكم الحاكمين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The reward suits the recipients’ innate preparedness, and their striving is appreciated rather than wasted through ostentation or reputation seeking.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : إن هذا كان لكم جزاء

words: إنا نحن نزلنا عليك القرآن تنزيلا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Qurʾān down in successive portions for wise reasons that required gradual revelation.
rows.anchor: أي مفرقا منجما لحكم بالغة مقتضية له لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the pronoun emphasizes that the Qurʾān is true revelation from the sovereign God, answering Meccan claims that it is sorcery or soothsaying and reassuring the Prophet not to heed their attacks.
rows.anchor: فإنا الملك الحق أقول على سبيل التأكيد إن ذلك وحي حق وتنزيل صدق من عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient while victory over the unbelievers is delayed; the outcome is good, retaliation should not be rushed, and every matter arrives at its appointed time.
rows.anchor: بتأخير نصرك على الكافرين فإن له عاقبة حميدة ولا تستعجل في أمر المقابلة والانتقام

words: ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منهم refers to the unbelievers; do not obey either a sinner calling to sin or an extreme disbeliever calling to disbelief.
rows.anchor: لا تطع كل واحد من مرتكب الإثك الداعي لك إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under a prohibition, أو distributes the ban over either of the two alternatives: do not obey one or the other, meaning do not obey either one.
rows.anchor: فكذا إذ قلت في النهي لا تكلم زيدا أو عمرا كان التقدير لا تكلم أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division concerns what the callers urge, since all are unbelievers; the general “sinner” excludes the specific sin of unbelief, the worst kind of sin, though a sinner may also be a follower and a disbeliever a leader.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا كفرة والكفر أخبث أنواع الإثم فلا معنى للقسمة

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qāshānī reads the command as remembering the greatest divine name through fulfilling its rights and manifesting its perfections in the beginning and end, from the rise of divine light to its setting and concealment.
rows.anchor: قال القاشاني : واذكر ذلك الذي هو الاسم الأعظم من أسمائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostrating to God for part of the night may refer to the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض اليل فصل له ولعله صلاة المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the time phrase first emphasizes night prayer because its greater effort and sincerity away from display merit special attention; the most difficult, sincere deeds are best.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الظرف للاهتمام لما في صلاة الليل من مزيد كلفة وخلوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف adds force as though the instruction were conditional: whatever may happen, prostrate to Him.
rows.anchor: ثم الفاء لإفادة معنى الشرط كأنه قال مهما يكن من شيء فاسجد له

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading makes prostration the annihilation of the self, bowing the annihilation of attributes, and standing the annihilation of actions, as the devotee worships through the night of nature and dusk of human embodiment.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : واعبد ربك المطلق حق العبودية بالفناء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means performing the night vigil, which was obligatory for the Prophet during a long portion of the night—two thirds, half, or one third.
rows.anchor: أي صل صلاة التهجد لأنه كان واجبا عليه في طائفة طويلة من الليل ثلثيه أو نصفه أو ثلثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the vigil “glorification” and placing its time phrase after the verb indicate that it does not have the rank of the preceding instruction.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير في التهجد بالتسبيح وتأخير ظرفه دلالة على إنه ليس في مرتبة ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ليلا is an adverb and طويلا its adjective; “long” does not distinguish it from a short night, since shorter night prayer is also covered, but signals prolonging the worship.
rows.anchor: فهو لتطويل زمان التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse returns to the Meccan unbelievers’ condition after consoling the Prophet with the revelation and patience passages.
rows.anchor: عاد إلى شرح أحوال الكفار بعد شرح صدره عليه السلام بما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They love the immediate world and immerse themselves in its fleeting pleasures; this, rather than uncertainty, drives their disbelief and refusal to follow.
rows.anchor: وينهمكون في لذاتها الفانية فهو الحامل لهم على الكفر والأعراض عن الاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وراءهم can mean ahead of them, where they make no preparation, or behind them, as something cast behind their backs; as an adverb it attaches to يذرون.
rows.anchor: أي أمامهم لا يستعدون فهو حال من يوما أو ينبذون وراء ظهورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وراء names a hidden or screened direction: the rear is concealed, and the unseen future ahead can likewise be called “behind/beyond.”
rows.anchor: وراء اسم للجهة المتوارية أي المستترة المختفية عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the day heavy transfers a property of physical bodies to an imagined duration, likening the day’s severity to weight.
rows.anchor: ووصفه بالثقل مع إنه من صفات الأعيان الجسمية لا الامتدادات الوهمية لتشبيه شدته

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines مرصاد as a place of watching, like مرصد, especially a place set aside for surveillance and waiting.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : المرصاد موضع الرصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the term may be generalized to a path that imprisons enemies and lets saints pass, the author prefers its application to unbelievers and the wretched, since surveillance at such a terrifying place is for punishment.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى لأن الترصد في مثل ذلك المكان الهائل إنما هو للتعذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: للطاغين may modify an omitted noun as an adjective of مرصادا, with مآبا in apposition; alternatively it may be a fronted circumstantial predicate of مآبا.
rows.anchor: ممتعلق بمضمر هو أما نعت لمرصادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A طاغٍ exceeds the limit in disobedience, transgressing in religion through unbelief and in worldly life through oppression.
rows.anchor: قالوا الطاغي من طغى في دينه بالكفر وفي دنياه بالظلم وهو في اللغة من جاوز الحد في العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the transgressors are polytheists, as the following verses indicate.
rows.anchor: والمراد هنا المشركون لما دل عليه ما بعده من الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destination is a return to which they will inevitably come; their punishment continues without end, unlike the finite punishment of a sinful believer.
rows.anchor: أي مرجعا يرجعون إليه لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: النداء means a sound; حديث here is the account of Moses’ encounter, which happened at the time his Lord called him, not a time governing the report’s arrival to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: النداء الصوت أي هل أتاك حديثه الواقع حين ناداه ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ may be construed as the time of the call or as the object of an omitted “remember”; construing it as the time the account came is impossible because the two events differ in time.
rows.anchor: لا ظرف للإتيان لاختلاف وقني الإتيان والنداء

rows.speaker: السجاوندي
rows.claim: Al-Sajāwandī marks a required pause after موسى, since continuing would make إذ govern the coming of the account, which he considers impossible; the author notes حديث is a noun meaning “report” here despite the preceding verb.
rows.anchor: وضع السجاوندي علامة الوقف اللازم على موسى وقال لأنه لو وصل صار إذ ظرفا لإتيان الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valley is blessed and purified by God when Moses spoke with Him; alternatively, it is called holy because it lies within the purified boundaries of the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: المبارك المطهر بتطهير الله عما لا يليق حين مكالمته مع كليمه أو سمى مقدسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وادي originally denotes a place where water flows, then the opening between mountains, and by metaphor a path, method, or style.
rows.anchor: وأصل الوادي الموضع الذي يسيل فيه الماء ومنه سمى المنفرج بين الجبلين واديا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: طوى may be read with tanwīn by construing it as a place, or without tanwīn as a locality; al-Farrāʾ prefers the declinable form because he finds no parallel for a name altered from its normal form, and takes it as the valley’s proper name and an apposition to الوادي.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء الصرف أحب إلى إذ لم أجد في المعدول نظيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طوى is identified as the name of the valley between Medina and Egypt.
rows.anchor: وهو اسم للوادي الذي بين المدينة ومصر فيكون عطف بيان له

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qāshānī reads the holy valley as the disembodied spirit-world, purified of material attachment; Ṭuwā is where bodies and souls are folded beneath its encompassing power, the realm of attributes and their theophany of speech, whose summit is the horizon where Muhammad saw Gabriel in his true form.
rows.anchor: قال القاشاني : الوادي المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is introduced as an implied divine utterance: “He said to him, Go to Pharaoh.”
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول أي فقال له اذهب إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنه طغى explains either the command itself or why Moses must comply with it.
rows.anchor: تعليل للأمر أو لوجوب الامتثال به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān is crossing the limit: Pharaoh transgressed against God by disbelief and against people by arrogance and enslaving them; ideal servanthood instead requires truth with God and good character toward people.
rows.anchor: وطغى على الخلق بأ تكبر عليه واستعبدهم

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qāshānī says Pharaoh manifested egotism: despite strength, wisdom, and learning, he became veiled in selfhood, claimed divine attributes and lordship, and so fell into tyranny and arrogance.
rows.anchor: وقال القاشاني : أي ظهر بأنانيته وذلك إن فرعون كان ذا نفس قوية

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying calls the worst person one upon whom the Resurrection has arrived while he is still alive; al-Qāshānī applies it to Pharaoh’s selfhood and self-worship as a veil in the station of oneness of attributes.
rows.anchor: فكان ممن قال فيه عليه السلام ، شر الناس من قامت القيامة عليه فهو حي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هل لك expresses willingness and inclination to accept the invitation.
rows.anchor: {هل لك} رغبة وتوجه {إلى أن تزكى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تزكى drops one of the two tāʾs of تتزكى.
rows.anchor: بحذف إحدى التاءين من تتزكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification means cleansing oneself of disbelief and tyranny, and of the opacity of human and natural conditions.
rows.anchor: أي تتطهر من دنس الكفر والطغيان ووسخ الكدورات البشرية والقاذورات الطبيعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لك is the predicate of an omitted subject and إلى أن depends on that implicit element; alternatively, هل لك is figurative for “shall I attract and invite you?”
rows.anchor: فقوله لك خبر مبتدأ محذوف وإلى أن متعلق بذلك المبتدأ المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offer is a figurative, gentle invitation rather than a blunt command, using a question to draw Pharaoh toward acceptance.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال قوله هل لك مجاز عن أجذبك وادعوك والقرينة هي القريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted genitive complement is understood: Moses will guide Pharaoh to knowledge of his Lord.
rows.anchor: وأهديك إلى ربك} وأرشدك إلى معرفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification comes before adornment: fear follows knowledge of God, and knowing God makes fear the goal of guidance.
rows.anchor: {إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماؤا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when God indicated Pharaoh would not purify himself, Moses asked why he should go; God ordered him to proceed, since twelve thousand angels in heaven seek knowledge of destiny without attaining it.
rows.anchor: فقال موسى فكيف أمضي إليه وقد علمت إنه لن يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is the essential outcome of guidance: whoever fears God does every good, while whoever feels secure dares every evil.
rows.anchor: وجعل الخشية غاية للهداية لأنها ملاك الأمر لأن من خشى الله أتى منه كل خير

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet’s saying that whoever fears sets out at night and whoever sets out reaches the destination illustrates fear’s role in attaining the goal.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : من خاف أدلج ومن أدلج بلغ المنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Moses to approach Pharaoh with an invitational question so tactful speech might draw him gently from obstinacy.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى أمر موسى عليه السلام ، بأن يخاطبه بالاستفهام الذي معناه العرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This unthreatening, detailed offer explains the instruction to speak gently in 20:44: it states neither polytheism, ignorance, nor disbelief, but what purification entails and where guidance leads.
rows.anchor: فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh recognized the sign on seeing it; his later claim that it was magic only displayed stubbornness.
rows.anchor: حين أبصرها عرفها وادعاء سحريتها إنما كان إراءة منه وإظهارا للتجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the signs to Moses reflects outward appearance, whereas attributing them to God in 20:56 reflects the ultimate reality.
rows.anchor: ونسبتها إليه بالنظر إلى الظاهر كما أن نسبتها إلى نون العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great sign was the staff’s transformation into a serpent; the other remaining miracles were lesser signs, and the sequence suggests this sign was shown first.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالآية الكبرى قلب العصاحية والصغرى غيره من معجزاته الباقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Immediately after seeing the great sign, Pharaoh called it magic and denied Moses without further inspection, reflection, or consulting reason and conscience, out of arrogance and rebellion.
rows.anchor: فرعون بموسى وسمى معجزته سحرا عقيب رأية الآية من غير رؤية وتأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He disobeyed God in extreme rebellion despite knowing the truth of the command, daring to deny the existence of the Lord of the worlds; the conjunction connects the sign’s effect to culpable denial.
rows.anchor: الله بالتمرد بعد ما علم صحة الأمر ووجود الطاعة أشد عصيان وأقبحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial is a verbal rejection despite inner certainty that the person denied deserved belief; denying someone not entitled to belief is not disobedience.
rows.anchor: وهو التكذيب باللسان مع حصول الجزم بأن من كذبه ممن يجب تصديقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading is that Pharaoh disobeyed Moses in what Moses ordered; the author says the denial of God is more effective in condemning him.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد وعصى موسى فيما أمر به إلا أن الأل أدخل في ذمه

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعرفة
rows.claim: Some spiritual knowers say that seeing signs rather than the lights of divine attributes left Pharaoh veiled from love and submission: witnessing attributes yields humility, while a vision of the essence produces insolence.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أهل المعرفة آاه آية صرفا ولو أراه أنوار الصفات في الآيات لم يكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh then turned away from obedience and from speaking with Moses; ثم marks a time interval because trying to undo Moses’ mission required time.
rows.anchor: أي تولى عن الطاعة وكلمه ثم على هذا معناها التراخي الزماني إذا السعي في إبطال أمره يقتضي مهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, أدبر means that Pharaoh left the gathering.
rows.anchor: أو انصرف عن المجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among creatures, the human being claims the greatest perfection: Pharaoh claimed lordship, while Iblīs disclaimed it and never claimed a station he did not possess; Iblīs has only majesty, angels pure beauty, and humans both, being created with two hands.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العارفين : لم يدع أحد من الخلائق من الكمال ما ادعاه ادعاه الإنسان

rows.speaker: ركن الدين علاء الدولة السمناني
rows.claim: Al-Sumnānī recounts visiting al-Ḥallāj’s spirit in a spiritual state and asking why Pharaoh’s “I am your highest lord” and al-Ḥallāj’s “I am the Real” led to opposite fates; the answer is that Pharaoh saw only himself and diminished God, while al-Ḥallāj saw God and diminished himself.
rows.anchor: شيخ ركن الدين علاء الدولة سمناني قدس سره فرموده كه وقتى مرا حال كرم بود

rows.speaker: مولانا
rows.claim: Rūmī’s verses distinguish Pharaoh’s “I am the Real,” which brings curse, from al-Ḥallāj’s, which brings mercy: Pharaoh’s I is stone and an enemy of light, while al-Ḥallāj’s is precious stone and a lover; theirs is arrogance, not union or incarnation.
rows.anchor: وفي المثنوى) : كفت فرعوني أنا الحق كشت ست

rows.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
rows.claim: One answer to why Iblīs was singled out for a curse while Pharaoh was not is that Iblīs’ intention was worse than theirs.
rows.anchor: قال في أسئلة الحكم فإن قلت ما الحكمة في إن إبليس قد لعن ولم يدع الربوبية

rows.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
rows.claim: A second answer is that Iblīs was first in initiating disobedience and discord in word, deed, and intention; later claims of lordship and oppression arose through his whispering.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأنه أول من سن الخلاف والشقاق قولا وفعلا ونية

rows.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
rows.claim: Iblīs confronted God directly in disobedience, while Pharaoh and others confronted prophets and intermediaries and sometimes confessed sins or supplicated to creatures; Iblīs neither confessed nor humbled himself.
rows.anchor: وإبليس واجه بمخالفته حضرة الرب تعالى وهم واجهوا الأنبياء والوسائط

rows.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
rows.claim: Iblīs was the first to institute disbelief and the direct source of misguidance, so the burden of disbelievers who follow returns to him until the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: فوزر الكفار بعده راجع إليه إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نكال means deterrent punishment that prevents anyone who sees or hears of it from attempting what leads to such a fate.
rows.anchor: الذي ينكل من رأه أو سمعه ويمعنه من تعاطي ما يفضي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نكال is used as a verbal noun of تنكيل, like سلام for تسليم, and is accusative as an emphatic cognate object.
rows.anchor: النكال بمعنى التنكيل كالسلام بمعنى التسليم وهو التعذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s punishment was drowning in this world and burning in the next; the phrase refers to both punishments.
rows.anchor: وهو الإحراق في الآخرة والإغراق في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخذ extends figuratively across worldly and afterlife punishment, since the worldly taking is literal and the afterlife taking figurative; the two abodes are named because the punishment occurs in both.
rows.anchor: وإضافة النكال إلى الدارين باعتبار وقوع نفس الأخذ
